Q Answer Skill Explanation and why the others are wrong Fastest method Common trap
3.1 B Textual evidence The claim is about expectation. B changes only what participants expected. A compares different people. C compares teaching with not reading. D is about preference. Underline "expect" in the claim, match it C, which is about actual teaching
3.2 C Words in context Spoke at length without committing: avoided the question. Candid is the opposite. Terse contradicts "at length". Emphatic contradicts "without committing". Read after the colon Terse, chosen because it sounds formal
3.3 B Sentence boundary Two complete sentences. A and D are comma splices. C is a run-on. Find both main verbs: "is" and "has produced" D. "However" does not join sentences.
3.4 D Transition The second sentence corrects a common belief. Therefore would mean the belief causes the definition. For example and likewise do not correct. Notice "many people assume" For example, because Antarctica looks like an example
3.5 -4 Vertex x = 10/2 = 5. f(5) = 25 - 50 + 21. Desmos, click the minimum Answering 5 (the x-value)
3.6 16 System shortcut Adding the two equations gives 4x + 2y directly. Add the equations Solving for x and y separately and losing time
3.7 A Exponential model Losing 12% leaves 88%. B keeps only 12%. C is linear. D is growth. 1 - 0.12 B
3.8 78 Mean Total 1440. Twelve students total 816. Remaining 624 / 8. Total = mean x count Averaging 72 and 68

Level 4 key

Q Answer Skill Explanation and why the others are wrong Fastest method Common trap
4.1 A Inference Fed crows approached, captured crows scolded, inexperienced crows did neither. The reaction follows experience with that mask. B fails: unfamiliar masks drew no special reaction. C fails: body type did not matter. D fails: they treated the two masks differently. Line up the three groups B, a plausible real-world belief
4.2 B Words in context "Far from" sets up the opposite of "strategist on whom leaders most relied": a minor figure. Pivotal is the same as the second half, not the opposite. Spot "far from", predict "minor" Pivotal, which fits the topic but not the logic
4.3 D Punctuation in a complex list When list items contain commas, semicolons separate the items. All separators must match. A uses only commas. B and C mix the two. See "Lyon, which" and expect semicolons B, which starts right and ends with a comma
4.4 C Weakening evidence The hypothesis says the lights removed insects. C shows insects increased and bats still fell. A and B are consistent with the hypothesis. D is too general. Break the middle link of the cause chain B, which looks relevant but supports
4.5 3 Quadratic structure ax + 3 = 6 or -6. So ax = 3 or -9. With x = 1, a = 3. Check: x = -3 gives -9. Plug x = 1 in first Expanding the square
4.6 2 Exponential f(4)/f(2) = b2 = 9, so b = 3. Then 9a = 18, a = 2. f(0) = a. Divide the two equations Treating it as linear
4.7 D Circle Radius = distance from (3, -2) to (7, 1) = 5. Only (-1, -5) is 5 away: 4 across, 3 down. Look for another 3-4-5 step from the centre Guessing by symmetry
4.8 B Percent of a subgroup Take 100 students. Girls who play: 15. Boys who play: 16. 15/31 is about 48.4%. Use 100 students 25% or 60%, numbers from the question
4.9 C Nonlinear system x2 - 6x + 7 - c = 0. Discriminant 36 - 4(7 - c) = 8 + 4c. Positive when c > -2. Discriminant, or a Desmos slider on c B, the tangent case
4.10 15 Trig sin A = BC/AB, so BC = 39 x 5/13. Scale the 5-12-13 triangle by 3 Using the side adjacent to A (36)

After each level

  1. Log every miss in Book 7, including correct answers marked G.
  2. Level 1 or 2 miss: find the careless-error pattern today.
  3. Level 3 or 4 miss: learn the method in the "Fastest method" column and redo it in 3 days.

Book 6

Full-Length Practice Tests

Which tests to use

All five full-length tests are the free official practice tests in College Board's Bluebook app. No test written in a document can stand in for them, for three reasons.

  • Bluebook is adaptive. Module 2 changes with Module 1 performance, exactly as on test day.
  • Bluebook gives a real scaled score out of 1600. Any conversion table written here would be invented.
  • Bluebook has the real interface: the timer, Mark for Review, the answer eliminator, the built-in Desmos.

If she has already taken some Bluebook tests, use the ones she has not seen. If fewer than five remain unseen, use the unseen ones for Tests 1, 4 and 5 and retake older ones for Tests 2 and 3.

Full-test schedule

Test Date Start Purpose Analysis
1 Fri Oct 9 8:00 AM Baseline Same afternoon, 2.5 h
2 Sat Oct 17 8:00 AM Check week 1 gains Same afternoon, plus Sun Oct 18
3 Sat Oct 24 8:00 AM Mid-point. Name the top 3 weaknesses. Same afternoon, plus Sun Oct 25
4 Fri Oct 30 8:00 AM Dress rehearsal Same afternoon, plus Sat Oct 31
5 Tue Nov 3 4:00 PM Final confirmation Wed Nov 4

Test-taking protocol

Every practice test is a rehearsal for November 7. Break one rule and the score means less.

  1. Same device she will use on test day, fully charged, with the charger nearby.
  2. Quiet room, door closed, phone in another room.
  3. Start at 8:00 AM for weekend tests.
  4. One sitting. Only the official 10-minute break between sections.
  5. Scratch paper and a pen. No notes, no formula sheet.
  6. Use the two-pass system and the clock checkpoints from Book 9.
  7. No pausing. No checking an answer on the internet. No extra time.
  8. Same breakfast and same snack she plans for test day.

Score-analysis framework

Do this within 6 hours of the test, while she remembers what she was thinking. Budget 2.5 hours. The analysis is worth more than the test.

Step 1: Record the numbers (10 minutes)

Fill one row of the score dashboard in Book 7. Then fill this grid.

R&W Module 1 R&W Module 2 Math Module 1 Math Module 2
Wrong
Guessed but right
Left for the last 2 minutes
Time left at the end
Felt easier or harder Module 2? n/a n/a

Step 2: Redo before reading explanations (45 minutes)

Redo every wrong question and every guess, untimed, without looking at the answer. This separates knowledge gaps from execution errors.

  • Right on the redo: the error was C, D, E or G. The knowledge is there.
  • Wrong again: the error is A or B. A concept needs relearning.

Step 3: Log everything (45 minutes)

One row in the error log for each miss and each guess. Follow the rules in Book 7.

Step 4: Count the patterns (20 minutes)

Count What it tells her
Misses by domain (8 domains) Which content to study this week
Misses by error code (A to G) Whether the problem is knowledge or execution
Misses by difficulty (easy, medium, hard) Whether points are leaking at the cheap end
Misses by position (first third, middle, last third of the module) Focus at the start, or timing at the end
Misses marked S (sure) Overconfidence. The most dangerous kind.

Step 5: Decide (15 minutes)

Write three sentences and tape them above the desk.

  1. "The three topics I will fix before the next test are ..."
  2. "The one habit I will change during the next test is ..."
  3. "My target for the next test is ... , which means at most ... wrong in R&W and ... wrong in Math."

Reading the patterns

Pattern Likely cause Response
Module 1 misses at 4 or more Rushing or careless reading Slow Module 1. Add the "what is asked" check.
Easy and medium misses exceed hard misses Execution, not knowledge Error codes C and D drills. No new content.
Mostly code A Content gap Back to Books 2 and 3 for those topics
Last 5 questions of a module mostly wrong Timing Stricter skip rule. Timed half-modules daily.
R&W misses clustered in grammar Rules not automatic Rules sheet daily. 15 grammar questions a day.
R&W misses clustered in words in context Vocabulary or not predicting 15 words a day. Cover the choices first.
Math misses on word problems Translation Write the equation before touching Desmos
Score flat for two tests in a row Reviewing answers, not errors Double the error-log time. Halve new questions.
Module 2 felt easy and the score is below 650 Routed to the easier module Module 1 accuracy is the whole problem

Rules for reviewing mistakes

About 30% of all study time goes to the log: 25 minutes on school days, 60 to 150 minutes after modules and tests.

  1. Same day. Log within 24 hours.
  2. Redo first. Attempt the question again before reading any explanation.
  3. Be specific. "Careless" is banned. Write "dropped the negative when distributing" or "chose a true statement that did not answer the question".
  4. Log lucky guesses. A right answer marked G is a future wrong answer.
  5. One prevention rule per error. It must be an action she can do during a test.
  6. Retry in 3 days. Cover the answer. If right, retry once more 7 days later. Two correct retries close the row.
  7. Wrong on retry. Reclassify as A, relearn the topic from Book 2 or 3, do 5 fresh questions on it.
  8. Weekly count. Every Friday, tally error codes and topics. Write the top three on the roadmap page.
  9. No new questions while retries are overdue. Retries come first each day.
  10. Read the "prevent" column the night before every full test.

What the weekly count means

Most frequent code The real problem Next week
A Content More concept time on the named topics
B Shaky method Worked examples, then the same question type 10 times
C or G Execution Slower Module 1 pace, one step per line, Desmos for arithmetic
D Reading the question Last line first, write what is asked
E Pacing Stricter skip rule, daily timed sets
F Hidden content gap Reclassify each guess as A or B

Book 8

Final 14-Day Sprint

Rules of the sprint (October 24 to November 6)

In the last 14 days the score rises by removing errors, not by adding knowledge.

  1. No new topics after Wednesday October 28. If a topic is still unknown then, let it go.
  2. Three full tests: October 24, October 30, November 3. Each gets 2.5 hours of analysis.
  3. Every session starts with the retries that are due.
  4. All practice is timed.
  5. Work only on the top 3 weaknesses named after Test 3. Rename them after Test 4.
  6. The rules sheet and formula sheet are read every day and written from memory twice.
  7. Sleep is part of the plan. 10:30 PM on school nights. No all-nighters for school work this fortnight if it can be avoided.

High-frequency grammar: the rules sheet

Write these on one page in her own words by October 25.

  1. Two full sentences: period, semicolon, or comma + and/but/so. Never a comma alone.
  2. Semicolon = period.
  3. Colon: full sentence before it.
  4. However, therefore, moreover: semicolon before, comma after.
  5. Extra information: two commas or two dashes. Never one of each.
  6. Essential name or title: no commas.
  7. No comma between subject and verb.
  8. Find the true subject. Ignore "of the..." phrases.
  9. Each, every, neither, either: singular.
  10. Its = belonging to it. It's = it is. Their = belonging to them.
  11. One owner: 's. Several owners: s'.
  12. Opening describing phrase: the thing described comes right after the comma.
  13. Lists and comparisons: same form.
  14. Tense follows the time marker.
  15. Transitions: decide same, opposite, cause or example before looking.
  16. Notes questions: read the goal, ignore the notes.

High-frequency Math: the formula sheet

  1. Slope = rise / run. y = mx + b.
  2. Standard form Ax + By = C: slope -A/B.
  3. Parallel: equal slopes. Perpendicular: product -1.
  4. System with no solution: same slope, different intercept.
  5. Vertex x = -b / (2a). Vertex form a(x - h)2 + k.
  6. Discriminant b2 - 4ac: positive two, zero one, negative none.
  7. Sum of roots -b/a. Product c/a.
  8. Difference of squares. Perfect squares.
  9. Exponent rules. xa/b is a root.
  10. Growth a(1 + r)t. Decay a(1 - r)t.
  11. Percent change = (new - old) / old.
  12. Total = mean x count.
  13. Random sample: generalise. Random assignment: cause.
  14. Triples 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17.
  15. 45-45-90: x, x, x sqrt(2). 30-60-90: x, x sqrt(3), 2x.
  16. Circle (x - h)2 + (y - k)2 = r2.
  17. Arc = (angle/360) x 2 pi r. Sector = (angle/360) x pi r2.
  18. pi radians = 180 degrees.
  19. sin x = cos(90 - x). SOH CAH TOA.
  20. Scale factor k: area k2, volume k3.

The final 72 hours

Wednesday November 4

Plan
Study Test 5 analysis, 2 hours. Write the last three traps to avoid.
Do not study New topics. Level 4 questions. Another full test.
Logistics Open Bluebook and complete exam setup if it is available. It opens a few days before the test and creates the admission ticket. Check the test-centre address and travel time.
Sleep In bed 10:30 PM, up at 6:00 AM. Start matching test-day wake time now.
Screens Off 45 minutes before bed

Thursday November 5

Plan
Study 90 minutes. 10 R&W and 10 Math, easy and medium, untimed, for rhythm. Read the rules sheet and formula sheet once. 5 minutes of Desmos.
Do not study Anything that produces a score. A bad set today proves nothing and costs confidence.
Food and water Normal meals. No new foods. Water through the day.
Logistics Charge the device to 100%. Update Bluebook. Print the admission ticket or save it on the device, as the ticket instructs.
Sleep In bed 10:30 PM, up at 6:00 AM

Friday November 6

Plan
Study 60 minutes before noon. 5 warm-up questions per section. Read the "prevent" column of the error log once. Then stop.
Do not study Anything after 2:00 PM. No late-night formula cramming.
Activity A walk or light exercise. Something enjoyable in the afternoon.
Food and water Familiar dinner, not heavy, by 7:30 PM. Water, but not a litre at bedtime.
Pack Passport or accepted photo ID, admission ticket, charged device, charger, pens or pencils, a snack, water, a watch without an alarm if the centre allows it, a light jacket.
Screens Phone away at 9:00 PM
Sleep Lights out by 10:00 PM. If sleep does not come, rest calmly. One short night does not lower a score.
Mental Read the three sentences from Test 5. Picture the first five questions going well.

What not to do in the final 72 hours

  • Do not take a full test.
  • Do not compare scores with friends.
  • Do not try a new strategy. Use what worked on Tests 4 and 5.
  • Do not change sleep, food or caffeine habits.

Book 9

Test-Day Playbook

Saturday November 7, 2026

The job today is to repeat Tests 4 and 5. Nothing new.

Before leaving home

Time Action
6:00 AM Wake. No phone scrolling.
6:15 Breakfast she has eaten before every practice test. Protein and slow carbohydrates. Normal amount of tea or coffee, no more.
6:40 Warm-up: 3 easy grammar questions and 3 easy Math questions. Do not check any hard question.
6:50 Bag check: ID, admission ticket, device at 100%, charger, pens, snack, water, jacket.
7:00 Leave so as to arrive 30 minutes before the time on the admission ticket.

Check the arrival time printed on the admission ticket. Late arrivals are not admitted.

At the testing centre

  • Use the washroom before check-in.
  • Connect to the centre's Wi-Fi and open Bluebook as instructed.
  • Plug in if a socket is near. If not, do not worry. A full charge lasts the test.
  • Do not discuss the test with other students. Other people's nerves are contagious.
  • While waiting: slow breathing, in for 4 counts, out for 6, five times.

Time plan

Reading & Writing (each module: 27 questions, 32 minutes)

Checkpoint Time left on the clock If behind
After question 9 22:00 Guess and flag the current one. Move.
After question 18 11:00 Go straight to the grammar and transitions questions at the end, then return.
After question 27 3:00 Use it for flagged questions, easiest first.

Math (each module: 22 questions, 35 minutes)

Checkpoint Time left on the clock If behind
After question 8 26:00 She is over-solving easy questions. Use Desmos or plug in choices.
After question 15 15:00 Flag anything over 2 minutes.
After question 22 3:00 Recheck flagged easy and medium questions first.

Reading & Writing Module 1

This is the accuracy module.

  • Steady pace. No rushing to bank time.
  • Question first, read once, predict, eliminate, prove.
  • For grammar: look at the choices first, name the rule.
  • Target: at most 2 or 3 wrong. Do not leave a single easy question unchecked.
  • Last 3 minutes: return to flagged questions. Reread only the question stem and her chosen answer.

Reading & Writing Module 2

  • If it feels harder, that is the sign she wanted. Expect 4 to 6 tough questions.
  • If it feels easier, do not conclude anything. Keep full accuracy.
  • Hard words-in-context questions: decide positive or negative, eliminate two, choose, move on.
  • Never spend more than 90 seconds on one question on the first pass.
  • The grammar, transition and notes questions near the end are still quick points. Reach them with time left.

The 10-minute break

  • Leave the seat. Walk. Washroom.
  • Eat the snack. Drink some water.
  • Do not think about R&W. It is finished and cannot be changed.
  • Do not look at a phone. It is not allowed, and it breaks focus.
  • Back in the seat with 2 minutes to spare. Three slow breaths. Say: "Write what is asked."

Math Module 1

  • Open Desmos at once and leave it open.
  • Read the last line first. Write what is asked on scratch paper.
  • Questions 1 to 10 are mostly easy. They are also where careless errors hide. Check each against what was asked.
  • For typed answers, check the sign and whether a fraction or decimal is wanted.
  • Target: at most 2 wrong.

Math Module 2

  • Expect the last 6 or 7 questions to be hard. Budget 12 minutes for them.
  • For each hard question, choose a route within 10 seconds: algebra, Desmos, plug in the choices, or pick numbers.
  • If no route appears in 30 seconds, guess, flag, move.
  • A hard question is worth the same as an easy one. Do not trade two medium questions for one hard one.

When to skip

  • R&W: after 75 seconds with two choices left. Pick one, flag, move.
  • Math: after 2 minutes, or when the third line of algebra shows no end.
  • Any question she has read twice without understanding what it asks.

When to guess

  • Always, before leaving any question. Never leave a blank.
  • With 60 seconds left, fill every unanswered question with one letter.
  • Typed Math answer with no idea: enter a sensible number from the problem's scale.

Handling a difficult question

  1. Breathe out once.
  2. Ask: "What is the simplest thing this could be testing?"
  3. R&W: eliminate one choice for certain. Then another.
  4. Math: try the choices, or put real numbers in for the letters.
  5. Still stuck at the time limit: guess, flag, go.

Recovering after a mistake or a bad patch

  • Every question is scored separately. The next one does not know about the last one.
  • A module that felt bad usually scored better than it felt. Hard-feeling modules often mean the harder, higher-scoring route.
  • If she realises an earlier answer was wrong and time remains, go back and fix it. If the module has ended, it is gone. Drop it.
  • Reset routine, 10 seconds: pen down, look away from the screen, one slow breath, read the next question's last line.
  • Some questions in each module are unscored trial questions. The strange one that made no sense may not count at all.

After the test

Scores for the November 7 test are expected around November 20. If the score is short of the target, the December 5 test (registration deadline November 20) is available. The error log carries straight over.
